articles.title: Ball Horticultural Company: Determination of Nonregulated Status for Red Flower Petals African Marigold (Tagetes erecta) Event pBALL123-022-BE113 3
articles.summary: We are advising the public of our determination that African marigold (Tagetes erecta) event pBALL123-022-BE113, which was developed using genetic engineering to produce red flower petals, is no longer considered regulated. Our determination is based on our evaluation of information and data submitted by Ball Horticultural Company in its petition for a determination of nonregulated status, available scientific data, the plant pest risk assessment, and public comments received in response to a previous notice announcing the availability of the petition for nonregulated status and a draft plant pest risk assessment. This notice announces the availability of our written determination and supporting documents.

articles.content: China P&I seeks seat at global insurance top table - Splash247 China Shipowners Mutual Assurance Association, better known as China P&I Club, has formally applied to join the International Group of P&I Clubs, potentially bringing a mainland Chinese insurer into the powerful marine insurance grouping for the first time. The International Group confirmed it had received the application after China P&I chairman Xu Lirong and other senior executives visited its London headquarters on October 13. “The Group was pleased to welcome CPI Chairman Xu Li Rong and other senior members of CPI to the IG’s London office,” International Group chief executive Nick Shaw said.“ At the meeting, the IG was presented with CPI’s application to join the IG, which will be considered in accordance with the agreed process.” The application will be assessed over the coming months against admission criteria agreed by the existing clubs. The International Group stressed that the process will not affect the February 2027 P&I renewal. China P&I is not starting entirely outside the system. The Shanghai-headquartered mutual is already an approved reinsured association within the International Group structure and has reinsurance arrangements with several existing member clubs. Full membership, however, would represent a significant step up in its position in the international marine insurance market. articles.content: Tsakos returns to containership contracting in China - Splash247 Hengli Shipbuilding Greek shipping group Tsakos has returned to the containership newbuilding market, emerging behind an order for two 3,200 teu vessels at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries. The pair appear in the Athens-based owner’s latest fleet register, with both scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2028. Both will be scrubber-fitted and equipped with alternative maritime power systems, allowing them to connect to shore-side electricity while alongside. Shipping database records point to contracts signed in September, although Alphaliner said the exact timing remains unclear and that the orders could have been concluded in August or September. Market sources put the ships at around $48m each, depending on final specification, implying a combined investment of about $96m. Neither Tsakos nor Hengli has disclosed pricing. Charter arrangements are also unknown. Alphaliner noted that Tsakos has typically backed containership newbuildings with forward employment, but there is no indication yet whether the Hengli pair have already been fixed. The deal marks Tsakos’ first return to boxship contracting since 2022, when the group booked a series of approximately 2,800 teu vessels at HD Hyundai Mipo in South Korea. articles.content: Falklands offshore development faces new international legal challenge - Splash247 Falkland Islands Govt The dispute over offshore oil development around the Falkland Islands has escalated, with Argentina seeking emergency measures from an international maritime tribunal while the UK moves to protect companies involved in economic activity linked to the islands. Argentina filed a request with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS), seeking provisional measures to prevent the UK from authorising hydrocarbon exploitation on the North Falkland Basin continental shelf. The filing forms part of an arbitration Buenos Aires launched against the UK under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Argentina argues that continued oil development could undermine its claimed sovereign rights and, while the dispute remains unresolved, risk serious harm to the marine environment. “The Argentine Republic reaffirms, once again, its legitimate and imprescriptible sovereign rights over the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas. By history and by right: the Falkland Islands are Argentine,” the government said in its statement. articles.content: MSC tipped for another 20 megamaxes in China - Splash247 Yangzijiang Shipbuilding Mediterranean Shipping Co (MSC) has reportedly added another 20 megamax containerships at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries, further expanding its already massive orderbook as global newbuilding commitments climb to their highest level in more than a decade. According to liner consultancy Linerlytica, Gianluigi Aponte’s carrier has booked 20 additional 24,000 teu vessels at the Dalian-based shipbuilder, representing another 480,000 teu of future capacity. The latest deal takes MSC’s programme of vessels exceeding 20,000 teu at Hengli to 62 ships, Linerlytica said in its latest weekly market report. No contract value, delivery dates or propulsion specifications have been disclosed for the new batch. MSC has built up a substantial pipeline at Hengli since the two companies signed a strategic cooperation agreement in 2024. The liner giant initially contracted ten 21,000 teu and ten 24,000 teu LNG dual-fuel newbuildings, before returning for six 22,000 teu ships last year. The latest reported order adds another sizeable block of capacity to an expansion programme that already dwarfs those of rival carriers. At the end of September, Alphaliner data cited by Splash put MSC’s operated fleet at around 7.4m teu, representing 21.5% of global liner capacity, with another 2.94m teu on order. articles.content: Spodumene shipments triple as battery boom creates new dry bulk trades - Splash247 Tata Motors The seaborne trade in spodumene, a lithium-bearing mineral essential for battery production, is emerging as one of dry bulk shipping’s fastest-growing niche cargoes, with volumes more than tripling over the past five years. New research from Greek shipbroker Ursa Shipbrokers shows global shipments reached 4.04m tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, up 11.9% year-on-year and a record for the period. Annual shipments have climbed from just 1.58m tonnes in 2020 to 5.08m tonnes last year, reflecting the rapid expansion of lithium mining and growing demand from electric vehicle manufacturers and battery storage projects. Australia dominates the trade, accounting for 81% of shipments during the first nine months of this year, equivalent to 3.26m tonnes. Brazil ranked second with 570,000 tonnes, while smaller quantities originated in Canada, Mozambique and Vietnam. China remains overwhelmingly the principal destination, receiving 88% of global seaborne spodumene cargoes, equivalent to 3.56m tonnes, reflecting its dominant position in lithium refining and battery manufacturing. The trade is providing growing employment opportunities for smaller bulk carriers. Ultramaxes accounted for 39.6% of vessel deadweight employed in spodumene shipments this year, with handysizes representing a further 46%. articles.content: Apache braces for offshore strike across seven platforms - Splash247 Apache More than 160 offshore workers, employed by US oil and gas producer Apache, are set to stage a 24-hour strike across seven North Sea installations on Wednesday, with union Unite warning the industrial action could disrupt the strategically important Forties Pipeline System. The walkout will begin at 6 am on October 21 and end the following morning. A second 24-hour stoppage is scheduled for November 4. The affected installations are Forties Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta, and Echo, alongside Beryl Alpha and Beryl Bravo. Unite said shutting down the Forties Charlie platform could drop pipeline pressure, potentially forcing the entire Ineos-operated Forties Pipeline System (FPS) offline and disrupting production from other North Sea operators. The FPS handles oil and gas liquids from more than 80 offshore fields and the St Fergus gas terminal, with a nominal capacity exceeding 600,000 barrels per day. Apache, however, has rejected suggestions that the strike could shut down the wider network. The company said contingency plans included retaining experienced personnel on Forties Charlie to support third-party production, even if output from all five Apache-operated Forties platforms was suspended. Apache maintained that any resulting pressure reduction would be comparable to a routine maintenance shutdown. The dispute centres on a pay offer that Unite claims amounts to a real-terms pay cut for many workers

articles.content: Despite new record, Port of LA chief warns of tariff-driven planning risk - FreightWaves The Port of Los Angeles moved 1.42 million TEUs in September, its best single month ever and the highest monthly volume ever recorded by a port in the Western Hemisphere, Executive Director Gene Seroka said this week. He said lower tariff levels, resilient consumer demand, and cargo shifting away from constrained Panama Canal and Suez routes drove the surge. Record quarter September imports totaled 546,000 loaded TEUs, up 19% year over year and 26% above the port’s five-year average. Exports rose 10% to 126,000 loaded TEUs, while the port handled a record 371,000 empty containers as carriers repositioned equipment to Asia. July through September was the port’s strongest quarter on record at nearly 3 million TEUs, and June through September moved nearly 4 million containers. Through September, 2026 volume stood at nearly 8.1 million TEUs, up about 3% from the same period in 2025. Seroka said the port expects October volume of about 900,000 TEUs. He cited typhoon-related schedule disruptions in Asia, cargo “roll pools” before China’s national holiday, and continued holiday-season replenishment as reasons volumes should remain elevated. articles.content: Mexico truck exports soar 145% as US demand accelerates - FreightWaves Mexican manufacturers produced 15,181 heavy-duty vehicles during September, compared with 6,857 in the same month last year. Exports totaled 12,707 units, up 144.6% from September 2025, marking a significant acceleration in cross-border commercial vehicle shipments, according to figures from Mexico’s National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) presented by the National Association of Bus, Truck and Tractor-Trailer Producers (ANPACT). The September rebound comes as Mexico’s domestic heavy-duty vehicle market continues to struggle with weak sales, delayed fleet replacement decisions and uncertainty surrounding U.S. trade policies. OK SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday reaffirmed South Korea's push to develop a new shipping route through the Arctic Ocean, saying it will be pursued in compliance with international norms and sanctions. The president made the pledge at a ceremony celebrating South Korea's successful voyage to Europe through the Arctic Ocean by a container ship, as the country seeks to operate summer-season container shipping services linking Asia and Europe. The PanStar Acro, a South Korean container ship, returned to the southeastern port city of Busan on Sunday after sailing via the Arctic Ocean north of Russia to Britain, the Netherlands and Poland, 50 days after leaving Busan. The pilot voyage marks the first successful trip by a South Korean container vessel via the Arctic Ocean, a route which is riskier due to polar ice, but offers faster shipping than routes via the Suez Canal. articles.content: Emarat Maritime piles six more tankers onto China orderbook - Splash247 Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry Dubai-based Emarat Maritime has added another six tanker newbuildings to its rapidly expanding fleet, lining up a series of 74,000 dwt LR1 product carriers in China. The company’s own fleet register now lists six LR1 newbuildings, with the first two scheduled for delivery in 2029 and the remaining four in 2030. Shipbuilding database records seen by Splash place the sextet at Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry. No contract price has emerged. Recent comparable Chinese LR1 orders have been running at around $55m per ship. Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend paid about $220m for four 74,000 dwt ships at Yangzijiang this summer, while Andriaki was linked to 73,500 dwt units at New Times at $55.1m each. On that basis, the Emarat sextet would benchmark at around $330m, although its actual contract terms remain undisclosed. The latest move significantly deepens Emarat’s exposure to the LR1 sector. Its operating fleet currently includes three older ships of roughly the same size — the 2007-built Dubai Diamond and Dubai Gold and the 2005-built Dubai Green. Delivery of the six new ships would therefore triple its LR1 fleet. The deal also takes Emarat’s overall newbuilding pipeline to 22 vessels. articles.content: Sweden frees sanctioned tanker after seven months - Splash247 Swedish Coast Guard Swedish authorities have cleared an EU-sanctioned product tanker to leave the country after nearly seven months at anchor following an investigation into its registration and seaworthiness. The Swedish Transport Agency has lifted an operating ban on the 2007-built, 75,000 dwt Sea Owl I, after confirming that the vessel is now legitimately registered in Equatorial Guinea. The tanker had been detained off Trelleborg since March 12, when Swedish authorities boarded it over concerns about its flag status and documentation. The ship was originally claiming registration in Comoros, which authorities found to be invalid. A subsequent attempt to establish registration under the Cameroon flag also failed verification. The Swedish Transport Agency said it had now received confirmation directly from Equatorial Guinea and had reviewed the certificates and crew documentation required for the vessel to resume operations. The decision removes the Swedish operating prohibition, although the tanker remains subject to EU sanctions. Sweden’s coastguard stressed that the vessel was not suspected of breaching sanctions. Investigations involving two former masters, including allegations concerning false documentation, have been discontinued. articles.content: The Heavy-Duty Oil Standard Is Changing In January, What It Means For Your Fleet, Your Costs, And Your Equipment - FreightWaves If your trucks have been running the same heavy-duty diesel engine oil since roughly 2017, whether you manage a hundred-truck fleet, run a small operation of a few units, or own the one truck you drive yourself, that oil is about to be replaced by something new, because the American Petroleum Institute is rolling out a fresh engine oil category called PC-12 that takes effect at the start of January 2027, and everybody who buys oil, specs it for a fleet, or just has it poured in at a shop needs to understand what is changing before it shows up at the next service interval. This is not a marketing refresh or a new label on the same jug. It is a genuine category change, the kind the industry only goes through about once a decade. The last one landed in 2016. Before that, 2006. So if it feels like you have been buying the same oil forever, that is because, in category terms, you nearly have. What is coming in January is a real shift in how these oils are formulated, what they are certified to do, and in one important case, which engines they are even allowed to go into. If you sit on the leadership side of a carrier, this belongs on your radar now as a procurement, budgeting, and equipment-planning item rather than a shop-floor detail to delegate and forget. articles.content: China completes world's first commercial green ammonia ship-to-ship bunkering - Splash247 CMB.TECH China has completed the world’s first commercial ship-to-ship green ammonia bunkering operation, transferring 1,000 tonnes of the fuel to Belgian shipowner CMB.TECH’s newly delivered Mineral Europa. The operation, carried out on October 13 and 14 at an anchorage off Zhoushan, saw the dedicated bunkering vessel Shenghang Yongle supply the 210,000 dwt bulker, the world’s first ammonia-powered dry bulk carrier. The fuel was produced using renewable electricity at China Energy Engineering’s Songyuan green hydrogen and ammonia project in Jilin province, before being transported through Nanjing to Zhoushan. The operation brought together China Energy Engineering, CMB.TECH and Jiangsu Andefu Energy Technology, establishing a commercial supply chain stretching from renewable fuel production to delivery onboard an oceangoing vessel. “The offshore ship-to-ship bunkering model offers remarkable advantages,” said Li Jingguang, chairman of China Energy Engineering’s hydrogen division, noting that future transfers could reach 2,000 or even 3,000 tonnes. Chinese maritime authorities supervised the operation, implementing special safety measures to handle the highly toxic fuel. Mineral Europa, delivered earlier this month, is heading across the Pacific to Australia for commercial operations. CMB.TECH expects 21 ammonia-powered vessels to enter its fleet by 2029, including 18 bulkers. TagsCMB.TE

articles.content: What Daimler's Finance And Global Chiefs Revealed About Diesel, Driverless Trucks, And The Future Of The Industry - FreightWaves On a rainy Saturday morning in Charlotte, inside the brand new North American headquarters of Daimler Truck Financial Services, four of the company’s senior leaders traded the usual press-conference script for something closer to a fireside chat, and over the better part of an hour they said more about where this industry is actually heading, from the engine under your hood to the driver who may one day not be in the seat to the rising cost of borrowing money against a truck, than most carriers will hear in a year of official announcements. The panel brought together a rare mix of global and local perspective. Eva Scherer, chief financial officer of Daimler Truck Holding AG, carried the worldwide view. Stephan Unger, chairman of Daimler Truck Financial Services, which operates across 21 countries, spoke to how the financing side of the business is changing. Kevin Bangston, president and CEO of Daimler Truck Financial Services USA LLC, handled the view from the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Goetz Johanning, head of strategy and realization for the North American financial services arm, moderated. The session was set up as a conversation rather than a presentation, and the candor showed. REUTERS/Khalil Ashawi U.S. to Allow Dark-Fleet Tankers to Shed Sanctions, Wright Says Bloomberg Total Views: 154 October 19, 2026 By Ari Natter and Annmarie Hordern (Bloomberg) — The Trump administration is authorizing the sale of sanctioned oil tankers in an effort to allow the vessels to start legitimately shipping crude, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said. The US government is working with investors who buy idled sanctioned tankers, refurbish them and use the ships to transport non-sanctioned oil, Wright said Monday at a Citadel Securities event in New York. “We’re going to move some of the ships from what I call the ‘bad-guy fleet’ to the ‘good-guy fleet,’ ” Wright said. “They will not carry sanctioned oil anymore.” Wright’s comments represent the first detailed public explanation from the Trump administration about turning to sanctioned tankers as it seeks to expand the number of ships available to transport crude and boost supply disrupted by the war in Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Ceva Logistics, a top-five global logistics company by gross revenue and part of Marseilles, France-based CMA CGM Group, acquired Paack in early August to expand its last-mile delivery business in Europe. It acquired Colis Privé, which also operates in Belgium and Luxembourg, in 2022. The unified Paack brand will be rolled out progressively to customers and partners beginning in January, Ceva said in a news release. When the tentative deal was first announced last summer, the expectation was that Colis Privé would absorb Paack. The combined business delivers 150 million parcels annually through a network of 17,000 out-of-home delivery points — 8,000 each in France and Spain, and 1,500 in Belgium. Paack has about 490 employees. It also operates six urban delivery stations in France. The couriers also deliver to individual residences. articles.content: European shipowners demand bigger share of EU carbon revenues - Splash247 ECSA European shipowners are calling for a threefold increase in the carbon allowances earmarked to support shipping’s energy transition, arguing that the sector contributes almost twice its share of emissions to the EU Emissions Trading System’s auction revenues. A study published by European Community Shipowners’ Associations (ECSA) estimates that the proposed Sustainable Maritime Alternative Propulsion (SMAP) mechanism needs at least 330m allowances, compared with the 110m currently envisaged by the European Commission. The association puts the required support at around €30bn ($33.6bn), aimed at narrowing the cost gap between conventional marine fuels and cleaner alternatives. The proposal forms part of the ongoing revision of the EU ETS and remains subject to approval by the European Parliament and Council. According to ECSA, maritime transport accounts for approximately 10% of emissions covered by the trading system but purchases almost 20% of the allowances auctioned.Unlike several industrial sectors, shipping has not received free allowances since joining the system in 2024. With the phase-in period completed, shipping companies must surrender allowances covering 100% of their emissions falling within the ETS framework from the 2026 emissions year. articles.content: China Merchants and COSCO move to exit Qingdao ore terminal - Splash247 China Communications Construction Company China Merchants Port and COSCO Shipping Ports are joining forces with IMC to sell a controlling stake in an iron ore terminal at China’s Qingdao port, setting a minimum price of CNY1.92bn ($287m). The three shareholders have launched a public tender for their combined 70% holding in Qingdao Port Dongjiakou Ore Terminal, according to Hong Kong stock exchange disclosures. China Merchants Port and COSCO Shipping Ports each hold 25% of the terminal company, while Singapore-based IMC owns another 20%. Qingdao Port International retains the remaining 30%. The stakes are being offered as a single package through the China Beijing Equity Exchange, with bidding open until November 11. The minimum consideration has been set at $287m, including $102m apiece for the holdings of China Merchants and COSCO. The terminal company is responsible for the construction, operation and management of iron ore handling facilities at Dongjiakou, one of Qingdao’s main bulk cargo areas. Dongjiakou has been developed to accommodate some of the world’s largest ore carriers. Its 400,000 dwt iron ore terminal entered service in 2013, giving the port the ability to receive very large ore carriers employed in trades between Brazil and China. articles.title: Evos raises $9M to build AI operators for industrial businesses
articles.summary:
Evos raised $9 million in pre-seed funding to develop AI operators that learn employees' workflows and perform tasks within existing business software. One freight brokerage has used the technology to make nearly 3,500 invoice-auditing decisions in two months, according to the startup.
The post Evos raises $9M to build AI operators for industrial businesses appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Evos raises $9M to build AI operators for industrial businesses - FreightWaves AI startup Evos raised $9 million in pre-seed funding to develop autonomous software operators for small and midsized industrial businesses, including freight brokerages, the company announced Wednesday. This comes as the company looks to automate routine work without requiring businesses to replace their existing software. The round was co-led by Uncork Capital and Field Ventures, with participation from Crosslink Capital, Utopia Capital Management, Sandwith Ventures and angel investors. Evos said it surpassed $1 million in annual recurring revenue four weeks after launching. The company did not disclose its valuation or the number of customers using its platform. How it works Evos is developing AI operators that learn how employees make decisions and carry out specific business functions within a company’s existing systems. Rather than requiring employees to prompt an AI tool for every task, the operators are designed to manage an assigned function independently once their decisions consistently match those of experienced workers. The approach targets smaller industrial businesses where operational knowledge often rests with experienced employees rather than documented procedures. articles.title: Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up
articles.summary:
Job boards show Tesla recruiting for Semi assembly, quality and service roles in Sparks as WattEV, IMC and the ZET SCALE alliance line up electric Class 8 orders.
The post Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up - FreightWaves Tesla had 103 job openings with Semi in the title posted at its Sparks, Nevada, truck plant as of Oct. 16, according to Tesla’s careers site. The listings come three weeks after the plant started high-volume Semi production on Sept. 24. The hiring is for a 1.7-million-square-foot factory designed to build 50,000 trucks a year, as fleets line up orders for a truck Tesla first showed in 2017. Tesla has not said how many Semis the plant is building now. Before the dedicated line opened, the Semi fleet numbered just under 200 pilot trucks, delivered to customers including DHL, PepsiCo and US Foods. Drayage carrier IMC Logistics ordered 50 Semis this month, following WattEV’s 370-truck order in May. Tesla was also named lead manufacturer on a 2,500-truck order through the ZET SCALE alliance in September, though the alliance did not say how many of those trucks will be Semis. Tesla CEO Elon Musk told analysts in July, “We have started production with the Tesla semi-truck.” The company’s second-quarter shareholder update said production was expected to begin later in the year. Semi openings span assembly to dispatch The Semi listings include quality technicians for stamping, body-in-white and powertrain; equipment maintenance technicians for general assembly and the drivetrain; and a CDL driver, a dispatcher and an endurance fleet driver. Several are night-shift roles, including a battery production supervisor

articles.title: Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels
articles.summary:
UPS has opened a larger air cargo and package terminal in the Philippines to better connect Asia with its global network.
The post Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels - FreightWaves United Parcel Service’s new air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines is 15 times larger than its predecessor, enabling the express carrier to provide up to two days faster delivery for customers within Asia and improve connectivity across its global network. UPS (NYSE: UPS) spent $80 million on the expansion project, which includes specialized handling areas for healthcare, high-tech and manufacturing customers with time-sensitive and temperature-sensitive shipments. Parcel handling capacity increased to an average daily volume of 46,000, with maximum processing capacity of 15,000 pieces per hour, according to a news release on Thursday. The announcement marks the first time UPS has disclosed the size of the capital expenditure to expand its Clark hub, which now covers 323,000 square feet. UPS now operates 170 flight segments into and out of Clark every week, connecting businesses across Asia Pacific, India, Europe and the United States in as little as one business day. The new hub has also created nearly 600 jobs, the company said. In August, the U.S. Department of Transportation approved the transfer of six UPS flying rights between Hong Kong and Warsaw, Poland, and Hanoi, Vietnam, to Clark Airport to support growing trade flows between the Philippines and Hong Kong. articles.content: West Africa's ore boom meets China's growing VLOC armada - Splash247 Winning West Africa is fast becoming dry bulk shipping’s biggest growth engine, with its mineral export boom poised to absorb the equivalent of another 120 capesizes by 2030. UK consultancy Tradeviews forecasts in a new report that shipments from the region will surge 50% from 2025 levels to 303m tonnes by the end of the decade, with Guinea’s giant Simandou iron ore project leading the charge. Crucially for shipowners, the long voyages to China will magnify the impact on vessel demand. “West Africa looks set to remain the fastest growing long-haul source of dry bulk cargo,” Tradeviews stated. The growth is already evident. The five West African exporters covered by the consultancy shipped 160.1m tonnes in their principal trades during the first eight months of this year, up 25% year on year. Liberian iron ore exports nearly doubled to 10.1m tonnes. Tradeviews expects regional exports to reach 267m tonnes next year, with Guinean iron ore shipments climbing to 45m tonnes in 2027 and approximately 112m tonnes by 2030. Bauxite exports, meanwhile, are forecast to retreat from a peak of nearly 194m tonnes this year to 153m tonnes by 2030 as Guinea pushes ahead with domestic alumina processing. A capesize round voyage between Guinea and China takes approximately 78 days, compared with just 29 days on the Australia-China route.
